propagation. Yeast rythems are considered  Ultradian metabolic cycles or cell cycle effects, not circadian (although fungi including N. crassa do exhibit circadian cycles)


* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).

see review

there is one 1989 report in pombe  under heatshock, but this is not considered true circadian.

Modern consensus emphasizes ultradian metabolic rhythms and condition-dependent phenomena in yeasts rather than a self-sustained ∼24-h circadian oscillator.

author: marcfeuermann
body:
I always feel uncomfortable when it's about PAINTing this term. As you mentioned, the literature is not clear. In this case, we have not much evidence and we have other more relevant annotations that could be used. 
Precautionary principle: I've remove the PAINTing. It is touching only a small node of this big family.

author: ValWood
body: I agree. It seemed odd to have only a single gene annotated to this proceess, (an endonuclease supposedly involved in rRNA processing) and nothing else at all!
